name: IsPointInPoly
formula: =LAMBDA(vertices,point,[isEdgeInclusive],LET(n, ROWS(vertices), x, INDEX(point, 1), y, INDEX(point, 2), isIncludeEdge, IF(ISOMITTED(isEdgeInclusive), TRUE, isEdgeInclusive), result, REDUCE(0, SEQUENCE(n), LAMBDA(acc,i, LET(j, IF(i = n, 1, i + 1), xi, INDEX(vertices, i, 1), yi, INDEX(vertices, i, 2), xj, INDEX(vertices, j, 1), yj, INDEX(vertices, j, 2), yt, IF(OR(y = yi, y = yj), y + ABS(y * 0.0001), y), isHorizontal, yi = yj, isYInbetween, AND(yt > MIN(yi, yj), yt < MAX(yi, yj)), intersect, IF(AND(NOT(isHorizontal), isYInbetween), x <= (xi + (yt - yi) * (xj - xi) / (yj - yi)), FALSE), IF(intersect, acc + 1, acc)))), isOnEdge, {ref}IsPointOnPolyEdge(vertices, point), isInclude_rayCast, IF(MOD(result, 2) = 1, TRUE(), FALSE()), IF(isOnEdge, isIncludeEdge, isInclude_rayCast)))
comment: Returns TRUE when Point lies inside the polygon. Vertices is an n×2 array of (x, y) rows in order; the last row connects to the first. Point is x then y, as a 1×2 row or a 2×1 column. isEdgeInclusive is optional and defaults to TRUE, so a point on the boundary counts as inside; FALSE returns FALSE for a boundary point. The test casts a ray toward +x and counts an odd number of crossings as inside. Fewer than two columns returns #REF!. Last Update at 2026-11-03.
